Added ESP applicability boundary; Database shares one mutable mutex and const find-based reads; socket deleter frees invalid-descriptor storage; removed throwing generic destructor rollback; corrected shared_ptr exception-safety claim. Made host socket acquisition exception-safe by owning allocated descriptor storage before socket(); scoped Rust read guard before write acquisition to prevent self-deadlock. Reduce the cross-language/desktop worked-example collection to firmware ownership, borrowed queue/callback storage, explicit failure cleanup and synchronization criteria linked to actual ScopedPreferences and FrameTxQueue code. Remove throwing/heap/POSIX, GCC cleanup, Rust and C++20/desktop skeletons rather than retaining them behind warnings; explicitly reject iterator/span bounds-safety inference and preserve NVS partial-save/timing limits. Keep original source identity/license and record this substantive specialization.

Added ESP32/API/version/scope boundaries and removed null metadata. Preserved reviewed hardware profiles; removed unsupported ISR/task/register-blink copy skeletons, including unchecked queue saturation, and references existing topic criteria instead. Scoped workflow/output to necessary changes rather than mandatory drivers/tasks or hardware execution. Clarify that an in-scope ISR defers to the existing foreground/task owner with SDK primitives, without requiring a new task.

Retained upstream RTOS topics with ESP-IDF byte-unit/framework-scheduler/SMP/volatile/private-config limits; removed unsupported task/queue/mutex/semaphore/timer/event/memory/notification skeletons rather than presenting unchecked platform/error-handling examples.

Retained upstream power topics with ESP32/scope limits; removed uncalibrated sleep/clock/peripheral/GPIO/ADC/battery/RTC/current-estimator implementations. Requires existing product safe outputs, actual hardware constraints and separately authorized measurement.

Retained upstream protocol topics; removed non-ESP register-level I2C/SPI-DMA/UART/CAN implementations, including unsigned timeout wrap and fixed eight-byte reads. Added bounded error/length/ownership criteria and existing production protocol/queue pointers; no replacement driver code.
